symptom: Two parallel `docker buildx build` runs of different projects corrupt each other's `RUN --mount=type=cache` content

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect cache mount IDs across Dockerfiles
diagnostic_steps.expected: id= field absent or shared between unrelated stages
shared cache mount entries with type=exec.cachemount

fix_steps.action: Give each cache an explicit, project-scoped id
For shared dep caches, use sharing=locked
fix_steps.validation: parallel builds serialize on cache writes

symptom: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=foo cat /run/secrets/foo` returns empty file or 'No such file' inside build

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify secret was passed to buildx
diagnostic_steps.command: # echo $FOO_VALUE | docker buildx build --secret id=foo,src=- ... OR --secret id=foo,env=FOO_VALUE
diagnostic_steps.expected: command line includes --secret with matching id

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm Dockerfile mount id matches CLI id

fix_steps.action: Re-issue build with --secret flag
For BuildKit cache export, ensure secret target read at RUN time only
fix_steps.validation: secret never persists into image layer

symptom: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` is 10-50x slower than native; build hangs or OOMs in QEMU

diagnostic_steps.action: Check qemu-user-static is installed in builder

fix_steps.action: Use a remote multi-arch builder farm with native nodes
fix_steps.command: docker buildx create --name farm --node arm64 --platform linux/arm64 --driver remote tcp://arm-host:1234; docker buildx create --append --name farm --node amd64 --platform linux/amd64
fix_steps.validation: buildx ls shows both nodes; build runs natively per platform

fix_steps.action: For one-off, accept the slowness or build per-arch sequentially
fix_steps.command: docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 ... && docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 ...

symptom: `COPY --from=builder /out/app /app` fails: 'invalid from flag value builder: stage not found'

diagnostic_steps.expected: line 'FROM <image> AS builder' upstream of the COPY

fix_steps.action: Add the AS-name to the upstream FROM
fix_steps.validation: docker buildx build proceeds past COPY

fix_steps.action: For COPY from external image, name the image directly

symptom: `docker build` fails 'COPY failed: file not found in build context' but the file exists on disk
error_patterns: file not found in build context

diagnostic_steps.expected: pattern that matches the missing file

diagnostic_steps.action: List what's in the context BuildKit sees

fix_steps.action: Add un-ignore pattern in .dockerignore

symptom: `--cache-from type=registry,ref=...` ignored; build always misses cache from registry

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm builder is authenticated to the registry
Check builder driver supports registry cache
diagnostic_steps.expected: docker-container driver (the docker driver does NOT support --cache-to type=registry)

fix_steps.action: Switch builder driver
fix_steps.validation: buildx ls shows docker-container as the active builder

fix_steps.action: Inject registry creds into builder
fix_steps.validation: cache hits visible in build progress

symptom: Dockerfile parser feature (heredoc `<<EOF`, `--mount=type=secret`) errors as 'unknown flag' on older builders

fix_steps.action: Pin frontend syntax version
fix_steps.command: # echo '# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7' to top of Dockerfile
fix_steps.validation: build pulls the requested frontend image

symptom: `docker buildx build -t app .` succeeds but `docker images` doesn't list `app`

diagnostic_steps.expected: docker-container or kubernetes (these don't auto-load into the daemon image store)

fix_steps.action: Add --load to push the image into local docker daemon
fix_steps.rollback: omit --load (image stays in builder cache only)

fix_steps.action: For multi-arch, --load is incompatible; use --push to a registry

symptom: `ps aux | grep containerd-shim` shows shims with no parent containerd; `docker ps` doesn't list the corresponding container

diagnostic_steps.expected: any shim re-parented to PID 1 = orphan
orphan PID NOT in containerd task list

diagnostic_steps.action: Check why containerd lost the shim (logs)
diagnostic_steps.expected: shim disconnect or crash near orphan time

fix_steps.action: Send TERM to orphan shim (it will reap container)
fix_steps.validation: orphan exits cleanly; container's rootfs unmounted

fix_steps.action: If filesystem layer remains busy, also delete via ctr

symptom: `docker run` (rootless) fails: 'newuidmap: command not found' or 'unable to set up uid mapping'

diagnostic_steps.action: Check binaries are installed and SUID-root
Check subuid/subgid entries for the user

fix_steps.action: Install uidmap package
fix_steps.command: sudo apt install uidmap   # OR dnf install shadow-utils

fix_steps.action: Add subuid/subgid entries

symptom: `runc create` fails: 'failed to mount /var/lib/.../rootfs: operation not permitted'

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm rootless or kernel restricts unprivileged mounts

fix_steps.action: Enable on Ubuntu 24.04+
For persistence, add /etc/sysctl.d/99-rootless.conf

symptom: `/var/lib/containerd` grows beyond expected size; `docker system df` shows much less

diagnostic_steps.expected: orphan blobs not referenced by any image

diagnostic_steps.command: sudo ctr -n moby images ls; sudo ctr -n k8s.io images ls

fix_steps.action: Run docker prune (covers moby ns)
For non-moby namespaces, prune via ctr

symptom: `runc list` shows a container stuck in 'creating' state for minutes; runc kill doesn't transition it

diagnostic_steps.action: Check runc init process is alive
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo runc state <id> | jq .pid; ps -o pid,stat,wchan -p <pid>
diagnostic_steps.expected: hung in a wchan that hints which step

fix_steps.action: Force-delete via runc
fix_steps.validation: runc list no longer shows it

fix_steps.action: If filesystem still busy, manually unmount the rootfs

symptom: `docker inspect` shows exit code like 137, 139, 143; user wonders what they mean

diagnostic_steps.action: Subtract 128 from the exit code → signal number
Confirm via dmesg if SIGKILL came from kernel (OOM)

fix_steps.action: For 137 + OOMKilled, raise memory limit (cross-link to docker.fm.exit-137-oomkilled)
For 139 (SIGSEGV), get a coredump from inside container
fix_steps.command: # echo '/tmp/core.%p' | sudo tee /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern; docker run --ulimit core=-1 ...
fix_steps.validation: core file captured for gdb analysis

symptom: `docker compose up` uses wrong env value despite setting it in `.env` or shell

diagnostic_steps.expected: resolved values that compose will apply

diagnostic_steps.action: List precedence order in your case
diagnostic_steps.command: # 1. CLI --env-file overrides .env; 2. shell env overrides .env; 3. compose service.environment overrides shell + .env; 4. service.env_file is read into container env (lower precedence than service.environment)

fix_steps.action: To force a value, put it in service.environment in compose.yaml
To pass shell env into container only when set, use ${VAR}

symptom: `docker compose up` doesn't start a service that has `profiles: [debug]` even with `--profile debug`

diagnostic_steps.action: Show effective config with profile flag
diagnostic_steps.expected: the profiled service appears in services

fix_steps.action: Pass --profile or set COMPOSE_PROFILES
fix_steps.command: docker compose --profile debug up   # OR  COMPOSE_PROFILES=debug docker compose up

fix_steps.action: Verify dependent services get implicitly enabled
fix_steps.command: # Profile-less services that another profiled service depends_on are still enabled

symptom: `docker compose up` exits before app starts: dependency 'service X' did not pass healthcheck within timeout

diagnostic_steps.expected: interval/timeout/retries appropriate for service start time

fix_steps.action: Increase start_period for slow-starters
Loosen probe (more retries or longer interval)

symptom: Two `docker compose` projects in different dirs collide because both default to network name 'default'

diagnostic_steps.expected: subnet that overlaps with new project's intended subnet

fix_steps.action: Set distinct project names
fix_steps.command: COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=projB docker compose up   # OR -p flag

fix_steps.action: Reduce default address-pool space

symptom: After host reboot, container doesn't auto-restart even though compose has `restart: always`

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm docker daemon restarts on boot
Confirm container's restart policy is in place

fix_steps.action: Enable docker on boot
Use unless-stopped to honor manual `docker stop`

symptom: App can't read /run/secrets/foo: 'permission denied' even though secret defined in compose

diagnostic_steps.action: Check the running user inside container

fix_steps.action: Set explicit mode + uid/gid in compose
fix_steps.command: # services: app: secrets: - source: foo, target: foo, uid: '1000', gid: '1000', mode: 0440

symptom: TCP traffic across overlay network drops or stalls; small payloads work, large ones fail

diagnostic_steps.expected: value vs underlay MTU minus 50 (vxlan) or 50+82 (encrypted)
see DF set; identifies max working size

fix_steps.action: Lower overlay MTU
fix_steps.command: docker network create -d overlay --opt com.docker.network.driver.mtu=1400 myover

fix_steps.action: For encrypted overlay, allow extra IPSec overhead

symptom: After `docker rename` or `docker network connect/disconnect`, other containers still resolve old name (or fail)

diagnostic_steps.action: From a sibling container, query embedded DNS

diagnostic_steps.expected: map shows current container names + IPs

fix_steps.action: Disconnect+reconnect containers to refresh embedded DNS records
fix_steps.command: docker network disconnect <net> sibling; docker network connect <net> sibling

fix_steps.action: For Compose projects, prefer service name (stable) over container name

symptom: `docker network create` fails 'all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted' or container fails to attach

diagnostic_steps.command: docker network ls -q | xargs docker network inspect | jq -r '.[]|.Name+" "+(.IPAM.Config[0].Subnet // "none")'
diagnostic_steps.expected: many networks consuming the configured pool
too small for current network count

fix_steps.action: Add more address pools to daemon.json
Prune unused networks

symptom: `docker run -p 80:8080` fails 'bind: permission denied' (rootless only)

fix_steps.action: Lower the privileged-port barrier system-wide
Or, use a high port and front with a system proxy/iptables rule
fix_steps.command: docker run -p 8080:8080 ...; sudo nft add rule ip nat prerouting tcp dport 80 redirect to :8080

symptom: With `--network=macvlan`, container can reach external network but cannot reach the host it runs on

diagnostic_steps.command: # kernel limitation: macvlan parent and macvlan children cannot communicate directly

fix_steps.action: Create a host-side macvlan shim interface
fix_steps.command: sudo ip link add macshim link eth0 type macvlan mode bridge; sudo ip addr add 192.168.1.250/24 dev macshim; sudo ip link set macshim up; sudo ip route add 192.168.1.0/24 dev macshim
fix_steps.validation: host can reach container IPs and vice versa

symptom: After running `iptables -F`, all docker port publishing breaks until daemon restart

diagnostic_steps.expected: chain present with DNAT rules per published port

fix_steps.action: Restart docker daemon to repopulate chains
Add custom rules to DOCKER-USER (not DOCKER) so they survive flushes by docker

symptom: Containers on user-defined bridge cannot reach each other; on default bridge they could

fix_steps.action: Recreate network with ICC enabled
fix_steps.command: docker network rm <net>; docker network create --opt com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc=true <net>

symptom: `docker run` on IPv6-only network fails to assign address; container has no IPv6 connectivity

fix_steps.action: Enable IPv6 in daemon.json with fixed-cidr-v6
fix_steps.validation: docker info shows IPv6: true; container gets v6 addr

fix_steps.action: Restart daemon

symptom: `docker run --security-opt apparmor=docker-custom` fails 'apparmor profile not loaded'

fix_steps.action: Load profile from file
Run container referencing it

symptom: Workload that runs natively fails inside container with EPERM on a syscall (e.g. clone3, io_uring_setup)

diagnostic_steps.command: docker run --rm -it --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined img strace -f -o /trace.txt ./bin

diagnostic_steps.expected: syscall not on allowlist for runtime

fix_steps.action: Run with --security-opt seccomp=unconfined (debug only)
For prod, ship custom seccomp profile that allows the specific syscall
fix_steps.command: # copy default.json, add {action:'SCMP_ACT_ALLOW',names:['clone3']}; docker run --security-opt seccomp=./custom.json
fix_steps.validation: workload runs with minimal added attack surface

symptom: `docker run --cap-drop=NET_ADMIN` and yet container can still configure network interfaces

fix_steps.action: Use cap-drop=ALL then add back only what's needed

symptom: `docker -H tcp://host:2376 ps` fails 'x509: certificate has expired'

diagnostic_steps.command: openssl s_client -connect host:2376 -servername host < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

fix_steps.action: Issue new cert and reload daemon
fix_steps.command: # regenerate via your CA tool; place in /etc/docker/{ca,server-cert,server-key}.pem; sudo systemctl reload docker

symptom: `cosign verify <image>` fails 'no matching signatures' even though image was signed

fix_steps.action: Re-sign with the right key
Pin image by digest in deployments

symptom: `live-restore=true` set, but containers still die on `systemctl restart docker`

fix_steps.action: Use `systemctl reload docker` for live config changes (not restart)
For real upgrades, accept brief outage or roll containers via swarm
fix_steps.command: # pin to swarm/k8s for true rolling upgrades

symptom: Container hangs on stdout writes after high log volume; `docker logs` empty or stalled

fix_steps.action: Switch to async + bounded buffer
For interim, fall back to local json-file

symptom: `docker node ls` returns 'no manager available'; swarm services stop reconciling

diagnostic_steps.action: Check raft state on each manager

fix_steps.action: Force a new leader from any responsive manager
Rejoin lost managers as workers, then promote
fix_steps.command: sudo docker swarm leave --force; sudo docker swarm join --token <worker-token> <leader-ip>:2377; docker node promote <node>

symptom: `docker exec -it <c> bash` works but typed keys don't reach shell

diagnostic_steps.command: # -i keeps STDIN open; -t allocates TTY; both required for shell

diagnostic_steps.action: Run with separate flags to isolate
diagnostic_steps.expected: if -i alone sees input but -it doesn't, terminal driver issue

fix_steps.action: Re-launch with both flags
If running through CI without TTY, drop -t

symptom: Bind-mounted shell script fails 'no such file' or '/bin/sh^M: bad interpreter' on Linux container

fix_steps.action: Convert to LF
Configure git to keep LF for shell scripts

symptom: `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` enormous; `docker system df` shows much less than disk reports

diagnostic_steps.expected: old layer dirs not associated with any image

fix_steps.action: Aggressive prune
If still leaked: stop docker, archive /var/lib/docker, recreate
fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl stop docker; sudo mv /var/lib/docker /var/lib/docker.bak; sudo systemctl start docker; (verify) sudo rm -rf /var/lib/docker.bak

symptom: `docker run alpine` on M-series Mac warns 'platform mismatch' or container crashes immediately

fix_steps.action: Pull explicitly for current platform
fix_steps.validation: docker image inspect shows correct Architecture

fix_steps.action: For multi-arch images set DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM

symptom: `docker pull` hangs or fails 'manifest unknown' after `systemctl restart docker` mid-pull; subsequent pull works

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect partial blob in content store

fix_steps.action: Re-pull (docker resumes via content-addressable retry)
If still stuck, manually delete ingest dir

symptom: With `userns-remap`, container writes files to bind-mount, host sees them owned by UID 100000+ instead of expected user

fix_steps.action: Pre-chown the host bind-target to match
Or, disable userns-remap for that container
